title: 1999 AMC 8 Problem 9
statement: Three flower beds overlap as shown. Bed \(A\) has \(500\) plants, bed \(B\) has \(450\) plants, and bed \(C\) has \(350\) plants. Beds \(A\) and \(B\) share \(50\) plants, while beds \(A\) and \(C\) share \(100.\) The total number of plants is

solutions.text:
Note there are \(50 + 100 = 150\) plants that are in two beds and there are no plants in all three beds.

The total number of plants is then \[ 500 + 450 + 350 - 150 = 1150. \] We subtract to get rid of the plants that we counted twice.

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Add the three bed counts first
Subtract the overlaps that were counted twice
